title: RAG & Retrieval
blurb: Retrieval-augmented generation from first principles: how to find the right passage, then how to use it.

anchors.note: Dense passage retrieval beat BM25 with a dual encoder and hard negatives. The paper that made dense retrieval credible.
Trains the retriever jointly with the language model rather than bolting it on afterwards.
The paper that named RAG. Parametric memory plus a non-parametric index, trained end to end.
Encode passages separately, fuse in the decoder. Still the strongest simple recipe for reading many passages.
Late interaction: keep per-token vectors and match them at query time. More expressive than a single vector.
Makes late interaction affordable through residual compression. The version people actually deploy.
Unsupervised contrastive retrieval that transfers without in-domain labels — the zero-shot baseline to beat.
Have the LLM hallucinate a fake answer, then embed that instead of the query. Absurd and effective.
Teaches the model when to retrieve and to critique what it retrieved, rather than always retrieving.
Recursive summarisation into a tree, so retrieval can operate at several levels of abstraction.
